What Is Rim Powder Coating?

Rim powder coating is a finishing process in which dry, electrostatically charged powder is sprayed onto a bare wheel and cured in an oven. The powder melts into a smooth, hard shell that suits both alloy rim powder coating and steel rim powder coating.

Unlike liquid paint, powder has no solvent carrier. The charged particles cling to the metal, then melt and cross-link in the oven, typically at 180 to 200 °C. That heat-driven reaction forms a continuous film that resists chipping better than most sprayed paint, which is why powder coated rims cope well with gravel, brake dust and winter road treatments.

People use wheel powder coating and powder coating wheels to describe the same job: refinishing the wheel itself. Frames, chassis and other vehicle parts belong to our [automotive powder coating](/services/automotive-powder-coating) page. This page covers wheels only, from one set of cast aluminum wheels to repeat orders of steel wheel refinishing.

Why choose powder over paint? Rim powder coating applies in a single controlled booth, cures without a solvent carrier and leaves a finish that is thicker and more uniform than most spray cans or brush jobs. It also reaches spokes, lips and barrels evenly, which is hard to do by hand. For most owners, professional rim powder coating is the simpler route to a finish that lasts.
How Does Our Rim Powder Coating Process Work?

Our wheel powder coating process follows six stages: inspection, stripping, surface preparation, masking, powder application and oven curing. Each stage protects the metal, and every wheel is checked before it leaves our Milton shop.

items: Inspection (on arrival). We check each wheel for curb rash, cracks, bent lips and corrosion, and we note any old coating. Please bring wheels without tires, valve stems, pressure sensors or balance weights, because the oven heat would damage them. Clear notes about the finish you want help us quote accurately.

Wheel stripping. Old paint, clear coat or powder is removed so the new finish bonds to bare metal. Heavy corrosion may call for our [sandblasting services](/services/sandblasting) before anything else happens.

Wheel surface preparation. Washing, degreasing and drying remove oil, brake dust and residue. Our [powder coating surface preparation](/services/surface-preparation) step is where a long-lasting finish is won or lost.
Masking. Wheel bolt hole masking, hub bore plugs and valve stem protection keep critical fitting surfaces clean, so the wheel still sits correctly on the vehicle.

Powder application. We spray your chosen colour electrostatically, reaching spokes, barrels and lips evenly. Clean, controlled application is the heart of rim powder coating, and it is why we keep this step separate from preparation.

Oven curing. The wheel cures at oven temperature, cools, and is inspected for coverage and smoothness. A full cure matters, because rim powder coating only reaches its strength once the powder has completely cross-linked.

blocks.text: Timing matters. Typical shop orders follow our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive wheels Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Forged wheel powder coating, two-tone wheels, heavy corrosion or large batches can need more time, so we confirm the schedule when we quote.
Which Wheels Suit Rim Powder Coating?

Most aluminum alloy and steel wheels suit rim powder coating, including cast and forged designs, provided they handle curing heat and have no serious cracks. Send photos and wheel details, and we will confirm suitability before any work starts.

items: Alloy wheels. Alloy wheel powder coating suits cast aluminum wheels and forged wheels. Cast aluminum can trap gases that cause pinholes, so we plan the preparation around the metal before coating.
Steel rims. Steel wheel refinishing removes rust and returns tired steel rims to a clean, uniform surface that resists new corrosion.
Other vehicles. We also take truck wheel powder coating, trailer wheel powder coating, ATV wheel powder coating and motorcycle wheel powder coating, whether you have one wheel or a full set.

blocks.text: To prepare for drop-off, remove loose dirt where you can, mark which wheel sits at which corner and take clear photos of any damage. Good photos let us quote rim powder coating accurately and spot issues early. We coat the surface, so structural wheel repair belongs with a qualified wheel specialist. If a wheel is bent or cracked, have it checked first and then send it to us. Our [capabilities page](/capabilities) lists size and weight limits for oversize wheels and heavy-duty wheel coating.
What Finishes Does Rim Powder Coating Offer?

Rim powder coating lets you choose gloss, satin, matte, textured, metallic or clear finishes, with colours matched to a RAL code or a physical sample. We help you pick a finish that suits the wheel design and how the vehicle is driven.

items: Popular looks. Matte black rims and gloss black wheels are common requests, and two-tone wheels add contrast between the face and the lip using careful masking.
Clear and metallic. A clear coat wheel finish adds depth over metallic powders and makes the colour pop.

Colour choice. Custom rim powder coating lets you move beyond stock colours. Our rim powder coating colours follow RAL references, and our [custom powder coating colours](/services/custom-colors-finishes) page shows the wider range.
Matching. Need a factory colour match? Send a sample or colour code, and we will recommend the closest powder.

blocks.text: Not sure which finish fits? Send photos and tell us how the vehicle is used. Our wheel restoration advice comes with every quote, and we will flag anything that could affect the final look before we start. Ask for a colour sample if you want to compare finishes before you decide. A short chat before coating prevents surprises and keeps your project on schedule.
How Do We Check Rim Powder Coating Quality?

We inspect every rim before and after coating for even coverage, a smooth film, clean masked areas and a complete cure. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, and test reports are available on request.

Preparation drives results. Coating over clean, bare metal gives better wheel corrosion protection, because the cured film seals the surface against moisture. Good road salt protection depends on that same bond, so we never rush stripping or washing. Consistent coating also means the next set matches the last, because we keep records that support repeat orders.

A fully cured film also gives a chip-resistant wheel finish, while an under-cured one stays soft. The smooth surface offers a brake dust resistant finish too, since dust is easier to wipe away than from rough paint. Together, these steps create a durable wheel finish that keeps its look through changing seasons.
To keep your rims looking sharp, wash them with mild soap and a soft brush, and avoid harsh acid cleaners. See our [certification page](/certification) to learn how we document our work.

Who Uses Our Rim Powder Coating?

Vehicle owners, trailer builders, farm and heavy equipment operators, contractors and fabrication shops send us wheels most often. They want rim powder coating that is dependable, fast and consistent from the first wheel to the last.

Trailer and equipment fleets suit [agricultural and heavy equipment](/industries/agricultural-heavy-equipment) owners, while crews from [contractors and construction](/industries/contractors-construction) often bring work wheels for rim refinishing. Larger repeat jobs fit our wider [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) work and the full range of [powder coating services](/services) at our Milton shop. Whatever you drive or operate, we treat each rim as a precision part and plan the coating around how it will be used.
Rim Powder Coating FAQs

Short answer: yes, most alloy and steel wheels can be refinished, and typical shop orders return in 48 hours. These answers cover damage, preparation, timing, paint comparisons and care before you book.

blocks.q: Can rim powder coating cover curb rash?
blocks.a: Light scrapes can usually be smoothed during preparation, which is how we handle curb rash repair on cosmetic damage. Deep gouges, cracks or bends need a wheel specialist first.

blocks.q: Do I need to remove the tires?
blocks.a: Yes. Bring wheels without tires, sensors, valve stems and weights, because oven heat would damage them. Rebalance the wheels after fitting new tires.

blocks.q: How long does rim powder coating take?
blocks.a: Typical shop orders follow our 48-hour turnaround. Heavy corrosion, two-tone work or large batches are scheduled when we quote.

blocks.q: Is rim powder coating better than paint?
blocks.a: Rim powder coating cures into a harder, more chip-resistant film with no solvent carrier. Paint can be easier to touch up, so we explain both options before you decide.

blocks.q: How do I clean powder coated wheels?
blocks.a: Use mild soap, water and a soft brush. Avoid harsh acid-based cleaners and abrasive pads, which can dull the finish. Gentle care keeps the finish looking sharp for years.

blocks.q: Can you coat only part of a wheel?
blocks.a: Yes. Masking lets us finish the face in one colour and the lip in another. Tell us the layout you want, and we will confirm what is practical for your wheel design.
